Spring Destinations: Where to Ride March-May

Spring transforms Britain. Grey winter landscapes burst into green, wildflowers carpet woodlands and meadows, and the riding season roars back to life. Here are the best destinations for each spring month.

March: The Early Bloomers

  • Cornwall and Devon: Milder than anywhere else in England. Daffodils line the lanes, and the coastal roads are rideable while the rest of the country shivers.
  • Wye Valley: Sheltered and mild. The river valley comes alive early, and the roads through the gorge are atmospheric in spring light.
  • South Downs: A gentle, rolling landscape perfect for a first spring ride. The chalk downland starts greening up in March.

April: Spring in Full Swing

  • Cotswolds: Blossom on the fruit trees, green fields, and the honey-stone villages looking their absolute best.
  • Peak District: The dales are green and the passes are clear of winter grit. Early enough to beat summer crowds.
  • Pembrokeshire: The coastal wildflowers begin in April. The cliff paths and coast roads are spectacular.

May: Peak Spring

  • Scottish Highlands: The best month for Highland touring. Long days, no midges, clear light, and empty roads.
  • Snowdonia: The mountain passes are open and the oak woodlands are full of bluebells.
  • Lake District: Before the summer rush. Daffodils at Ullswater, green fells, and quiet roads.
  • Yorkshire Dales: The hay meadows begin their spectacular wildflower display.

Spring Riding Tips

  • Layer your clothing — spring temperatures can vary 15°C in a single day.
  • Watch for lambs near roads in March and April.
  • Road surfaces may still have winter grit and debris in corners — ride smoothly.
  • Carry waterproofs — April showers are real and frequent.
  • Start with shorter rides and build up distance as your fitness returns after winter.
Spring riding is the most optimistic motorcycling of the year. Every ride feels like a rediscovery. The roads are familiar but the landscape is transformed. Savour the freshness — by July, you'll take it for granted.

Winter Charity Rides

The Christmas period sees some of the UK's most heartwarming motorcycle events. Toy runs — where bikers carry wrapped presents to children's hospitals and charities — happen in most UK regions during December. These organised rides combine the joy of riding with genuine charitable impact.

The Distinguished Gentleman's Ride occurs in September, but many informal charity rides happen through the winter months. Local clubs organise collections for food banks, homeless shelters, and other causes. These rides provide both social connection and a sense of purpose during the darker months of the year.

Winter Social Riding

The Christmas period is one of the most social times in the motorcycle calendar. Toy runs bring hundreds of riders together for charity in a festive atmosphere. Boxing Day meets at pubs and cafés are traditions in many areas — check local motorcycle forums and Facebook groups for events near you.

New Year's Day gatherings at famous biker stops draw enthusiastic crowds. The Ace Café in London, Squires Café in Yorkshire, and Matlock Bath in the Peak District all see significant numbers of riders on January 1st, regardless of weather. The atmosphere is optimistic and forward-looking — a perfect way to kick off the riding year.

If you prefer quieter riding, Twixmas (December 27-30) often delivers surprisingly mild weather and deserted roads. Everyone is at home digesting leftovers while you have the countryside to yourself. A Twixmas ride through the lanes, finishing at a pub for a restorative lunch, is one of the winter's quiet pleasures. Read our UK Motorcycle Riding in February: First Signs of Spring guide for more. keyTakeaways: Spring transforms Britain from March to May, with wildflowers and the riding season roaring back to life.
March favours mild Cornwall, Devon, the sheltered Wye Valley and the South Downs.
April brings the Cotswolds, Peak District and Pembrokeshire into their own.
May is peak spring, with the Scottish Highlands, Snowdonia, Lake District and Yorkshire Dales at their best.
Layer clothing, watch for lambs, expect April showers and build distance gradually after winter.

faq.q: Where should I ride in early spring in March?
faq.a: March suits the early bloomers. Cornwall and Devon are milder than anywhere else in England, with daffodils lining the lanes and rideable coastal roads. The Wye Valley is sheltered and mild, coming alive early with atmospheric roads through the gorge. The South Downs offer a gentle, rolling landscape that greens up in March, perfect for a first spring ride.

faq.q: What are the best April spring destinations?
faq.a: April sees spring in full swing. The Cotswolds show blossom on the fruit trees and honey-stone villages at their best, the Peak District dales are green with passes clear of winter grit, and Pembrokeshire's coastal wildflowers begin, making the cliff paths and coast roads spectacular. It is early enough to beat the summer crowds across all three.

faq.q: Why is May the peak of spring riding?
faq.a: May is peak spring, when the Scottish Highlands are at their best with long days, no midges, clear light and empty roads. Snowdonia's mountain passes are open and its oak woodlands are full of bluebells, the Lake District offers daffodils at Ullswater and quiet roads before the summer rush, and the Yorkshire Dales begin their spectacular hay-meadow wildflower display.

faq.q: What should I pack for spring riding?
faq.a: Layer your clothing because spring temperatures can vary by 15C in a single day. Carry waterproofs, since April showers are real and frequent. Watch for lambs near roads in March and April, and ride smoothly because road surfaces may still hold winter grit and debris in corners. Start with shorter rides and build up distance as your fitness returns after winter.

faq.q: Why is spring such optimistic riding?
faq.a: Spring is the most optimistic motorcycling of the year because every ride feels like a rediscovery. The roads are familiar but the landscape is transformed, with grey winter giving way to green and wildflowers carpeting woodlands and meadows. Savour the freshness of those first rides through daffodils, blossom and bluebells, because by July you will take the greenery for granted.
